expectations.text: Flags the line `db.query(\`SELECT * FROM orders WHERE user_id = ${req.params.id}\`)` as a SQL injection risk and quotes the vulnerable line in the finding
expectations.evidence: Quotes the line in a fenced block under '**Critical — SQL injection (line 5)**'.

expectations.text: Names `req.params.id` as the untrusted/user-controlled input source for the injection finding
Identifies the `for (const order of orders)` loop calling `db.orderItem.findMany` as an N+1 query pattern
Proposes a fix for the N+1 using `include` on the initial order query or a single batched `findMany` with an `in` filter, rather than the per-order query
expectations.evidence: Proposes the Prisma include fix with code.

expectations.text: Flags `prisma.event.findMany()` in `listEvents` as unbounded and proposes a concrete `take` value or pagination as the fix
expectations.evidence: 'prisma.event.findMany() with no take/cursor pulls the whole table on every call. Add pagination and a select' — satisfies the pagination branch of the assertion.

expectations.text: Does not flag `db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $1', [userId])` in `getUserById` as an injection risk
expectations.evidence: '**Minor — getUserById (line 22)** Parameterized ($1) so no injection risk'. Also correctly declines to flag the parameterized Prisma call.
